evidence.quote: Sign up for a free account to build on the Xero platform.
Xero's API supports the authorization code grant type using the standard authorization code flow or the PKCE extension; Custom Connections use the client_credentials grant type
224 endpoints (Accounting API alone; Xero also exposes Payroll, Assets, Files, Projects, Practice Manager, Bank Feeds APIs)
An MCP server that integrates with the MCP protocol.
using a Demo Company to start with because it comes with some pre-loaded sample data
our platform remains free for internal innovation

result.notes: Xero (developer.xero.com) offers free self-serve developer accounts with a sandbox "Demo Company" for building/testing against the Accounting, Payroll, Assets, Files, Projects and other REST APIs via OAuth2 (authorization code + PKCE). A separate "Custom Connections" option uses the OAuth2 client_credentials grant for non-interactive/tenant-to-tenant integrations but is described as a "premium integration option" tied to the connected org's Xero subscription plan — this only gates that specific non-interactive flow, not general API access. Publishing an app publicly on the Xero App Store additionally requires app partner certification (e.g., reference customers), but that gates marketplace distribution, not developer/API access itself. Xero publishes an official MCP server (XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server) supporting both custom-connection and bearer-token auth modes. Several JS-rendered doc pages (oauth2/overview, auth-flow, getting-started-guide) returned only page titles to the fetch tool; auth-method and access details were cross-verified via search-engine cache of those same pages plus the GitHub MCP repo and the precomputed API probe.
result.one_liner: Xero is a cloud accounting/bookkeeping platform exposing REST APIs (Accounting, Payroll, Assets, Files, Projects, etc.) for invoicing, contacts, bank reconciliation and financial reporting.
